title: Cold first paint, path A (direct load, intro-gated)

raw.label: RTH CERTIFYING RUN

per_run.swap_reason: uptime unreadable (health 502 during a swap reads like this)

raw.parts_served_from_cache_vs_built: NOT SEPARABLE from the client. The rig records which parts were SERVED and at which version, but the response carries no cache-hit marker the browser can read. Server-side, stats_process_local.build_failures stayed 0 and the parts cache stayed at 10 throughout (item 5), and no roll reported a miss.
raw.version_at_paint_vs_current: every valid run painted at the then-current version; run 3 saw the version advance mid-load (29823243 -> 29823244) and still painted

intro_animation_share.method: the rig exposes no intro-duration field, so the intro's share cannot be read directly from a path-A run. It is inferred by differencing the two paths measured on the same tape in the same half hour: path A median 10104 ms (intro plays) minus path B median shell 542 ms (no intro) = ~9562 ms.
intro_animation_share.corroboration: CLAUDE.md documents the intro as a ~9.3 s three-act animation, which the ~9.56 s difference is consistent with
intro_animation_share.page_own_cost_without_intro: use path B (item 10): shell 542 ms median, picks 2020 ms median. Those ARE measured, and they are the honest 'page on its own' numbers.

guards.guard: pod age >= 120 s on every counted run
guards.observed: 1991-2179 s across runs 2-6; run 1 had an unreadable uptime and was discarded

guards.guard: no deploy during the counted runs
guards.observed: deploy_swapped=false on all 5 counted runs; uptime rose monotonically 1991 -> 2179 s. The sampler confirms independently that the only restart of the session was at 09:30:31 ET, 37 minutes before these runs.

guards.guard: the discarded run was discarded for cause, not to improve the number
guards.observed: run 1 was rejected BY THE RIG, not by me, on uptime being unreadable behind a transient 502. Its first_content was 67434 ms -- an outlier 4x the worst counted run -- so excluding it flatters the result, and it is reported here in full rather than dropped.

guards.guard: fewer than half the runs rejected (no re-run required)
guards.observed: 1 of 6 rejected, below the half threshold

guards.guard: runs spread across the roll cycle
guards.observed: Runs were issued back to back rather than deliberately phased against the ~60 s roll cycle. Their start times and durations do spread them across different phases -- run 3 caught a mid-load version advance, which is the just-before-a-roll case -- but this was incidental coverage, not the designed sampling the item asks for.
the rig asserts visibility at runtime; all runs produced flow requests, which cannot happen in a hidden tab

notes: Path A median first content is 10.1 s, worst 16.2 s, and roughly 9.5 s of that is the intro animation rather than the page. The page's own cost is item 10's number, not this one. Two observations worth carrying: (1) wire bytes vary 6x across runs on the same tape -- 28 KB, 56 KB, 143 KB, 145 KB, 815 KB -- and the two cheapest runs served only TOP_PICKS + bootstrap while the expensive ones also pulled CONV + TICKER_DB, so the transport is doing materially different work run to run; (2) run 1's 67 s is not counted but should not be forgotten -- a member hitting the same transient would have waited over a minute for first content.
